payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce electrolyte crossover, a major aging mechanism in sodium-flow designs. Its measured gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, and projected stack-level cost at 500 MWh manufacturing scale is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte. Following an independent audit, the governing cycle-life result is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because of un-normalized depth-of-discharge.
